[SPIKE] Research and implement guardrails to prevent direct-to-main pushes by agents. Incident: commits cbbfb81 and 3fd285a were pushed directly to main bypassing branch protection after a PR merge. Research scope: (1) git pre-push hooks that block pushes to main locally, (2) GitHub branch protection hardening (require PR, disable admin bypass for agents), (3) agent-level instruction/checklist enforcement in copilot-instructions.md, (4) CI workflow to detect and alert on direct main commits. Deliverable: a recommendation with the lowest-friction approach that works for both human and agent contributors, plus implementation.

PDF document ingestion: add ability to parse and chunk PDF files of any size into the pipeline. Requires: PDF text extraction crate (evaluate pdf-extract, lopdf, pdfium), page/section-aware chunking strategy, handling of tables/images/figures (text extraction vs OCR), large-file streaming to avoid memory blowout, integration as a new parser backend alongside Markdown. Needs a spike to evaluate crate choices, extraction quality, and chunking strategy for structured documents.
Fix stale doc comment in src/chunk/mod.rs:5 — still references "LanceDB vectors to Kùzu graph nodes" but should reference CozoDB unified store

Persist embeddings in CozoDB HNSW index and implement semantic vector search (search_similar). Currently vectors are computed during sync but discarded. This is the primary value-add — enabling similarity-based documentation discovery beyond keyword matching. Planned internally as 009-F.

Expand MCP tool surface: add list_sources (enumerate indexed sources), get_chunk_by_id (retrieve chunk by SHA-256 ID), get_document (all chunks for a path), search_semantic (vector search, depends on HNSW), get_status (DB stats/health). Currently only search_local_docs and traverse_doc_links exist.

Wire incremental sync (sync_source) into the CLI sync command. The sync module exists and is tested (git diff + mtime diff + surgical re-ingestion) but cmd_sync uses the full pipeline::run instead. Add --full flag for existing behavior, make incremental the default.

Web crawler acquisition source: add type: url source to sources.yaml for crawling live documentation sites (e.g. learn.microsoft.com/azure/cosmos-db/). Requires: HTTP client (reqwest), HTML-to-Markdown converter, recursive link follower with configurable depth/domain limits, rate limiting, robots.txt compliance, deduplication. This is a new acquisition backend alongside git and local — follows the same pipeline interface (returns list of Markdown files for parse stage). Needs a spike first to evaluate crate choices and crawl strategy.

Word document (.docx) ingestion: add ability to parse and chunk Word documents of any size into the pipeline. Requires: OOXML parser crate (evaluate docx-rs, office-crypto, or zip + xml manual parsing), paragraph/heading-aware chunking, table extraction, embedded image handling, large-file streaming, integration as a new parser backend alongside Markdown and PDF. Needs a spike to evaluate crate choices, extraction fidelity, and chunking strategy for Word's nested structure.

E2E smoke test: configure sources.yaml with azure-cosmos-db-docs repo, run graphtor-docs sync, verify chunks loaded with graphtor-docs status, start MCP server with graphtor-docs serve, test search_local_docs and traverse_doc_links against real Cosmos DB documentation content.

Agent harness learning: Stage agent MUST NOT call backlogit_ship_shipment, backlogit_claim_shipment, backlogit_archive_item, or backlogit_delete_item. Stage only assembles shipments and gates readiness (verifies tasks are decomposed, plans reviewed, tests defined). Ship agent owns: claiming the shipment, feature branch creation, build loop, PR lifecycle, CI validation, review handling, operator-approved merge, and THEN backlogit_ship_shipment. Stage's terminal action is confirming readiness and reporting to the operator for Ship orchestration.

Mature the documentation source registry (sources.yaml) to support mixed-format ingestion per source: each Git, URL, or local source entry should declare which document types it contains (PDF, DOCX, Markdown) so the pipeline dispatches the correct parser per file. Add schema validation, default format lists, and per-source format override configuration. This enables a single Git repo source to ingest its Markdown, PDF, and DOCX files in one pass.

Fully test PDF, DOCX, and Git repo documentation ingestion: create comprehensive integration tests covering each acquisition source type end-to-end (acquire → parse → chunk → embed → load). Validate correct handling of edge cases (large files, malformed input, empty documents, nested structures) for each format. Ensure deterministic chunk IDs and idempotent re-ingestion across all three source types.

Streaming PDF parser with heading-aware chunk accumulation: Replace current whole-file PDF parsing with page-streaming via lopdf (random page access). Stream pages one at a time, detect heading boundaries via font-size heuristics, accumulate text into section buffers, and emit chunks at semantic boundaries rather than arbitrary page breaks. This bounds memory usage (one section at a time vs. entire PDF), produces semantically meaningful chunks aligned to document structure, avoids near-duplicate chunks from overlapping page windows, and naturally fits the existing doc_chunks schema (headings, content, position). Requires evaluating lopdf vs pdf-extract for font metadata access. Current pdf-extract approach loads entire PDF and produces flat text with no heading detection — debug-mode processing of a 109MB PDF takes 45+ minutes.

PDFium-render dual backend for large PDF ingestion: Replace pdf-extract with pdfium-render for PDFs ≥20 MiB. PDFium opens documents lazily (instant for any size) vs pdf-extract's lopdf which eagerly parses all xref entries serially (>20 min for 104 MB). Implementation: PdfiumBackend struct with try_parse() fallback pattern, DLL discovery via env var → exe dir → system path. Already benchmarked: pdf-extract DNF on Cosmos DB PDF, pdfium-render expected <10s. Dependency: pdfium-render 0.9.1 (thread_safe, pdfium_latest features). Feature branch exists: feat/pdfium-large-pdf-backend with partial implementation.

Comprehensive documentation for all aspects of graphtor-docs: architecture overview, data pipeline stages (acquire/parse/embed/load), MCP tool reference, configuration guide (sources.yaml schema, all source types), CLI command reference, developer setup guide, embedding model details (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 via Candle), CozoDB schema and query patterns, incremental sync design, and troubleshooting guide. Should cover both user-facing (how to configure and run) and developer-facing (how to contribute and extend) perspectives. Output: docs/ directory with well-structured markdown files.

Refactor PdfExtractBackend Pass 2 to use output_doc_page in a page-by-page loop instead of output_doc (full traversal), enabling heading-aware chunking for PDFs of any size. Currently the 20 MiB LARGE_PDF_THRESHOLD guard forces all large PDFs into page-based chunking with heading_hierarchy: ["Page N"]. The histogram (Pass 1) is already bounded at 30 pages and is not the bottleneck — Pass 2 is. Switching Pass 2 to output_doc_page makes the threshold guard unnecessary and restores section-based chunk IDs for large PDFs. Analysis: docs/research/pdf-pass2-page-by-page-refactor-2026-05-04.md

Rebrand MCP tool names to be source-agnostic: rename `search_ms_docs_semantic` → `search_semantic`, ensure tool descriptions don't imply MS-only scope. The underlying engine already handles any Markdown source — the naming is the only barrier to multi-workspace adoption.

Add pre-sync commands to start.ps1: run `graphtor-docs sync` and `backlogit sync` before launching copilot. Ensures both the doc index and backlog index are fresh at session start without relying on the agent or operator to remember. Complements the auto-sync-on-serve feature but works immediately without code changes to graphtor itself.

Workspace auto-discovery mode: graphtor automatically detects and indexes .md files in the current repo without requiring manual sources.yaml configuration. Enables zero-config adoption in any workspace — just run `graphtor-docs install && graphtor-docs sync` and it indexes the local repo's docs.

Auto-sync on MCP server start: when `graphtor-docs serve` launches the MCP server, it should detect stale or unsynced content (via commit hash / mtime comparison) and perform an incremental sync before accepting tool calls. Eliminates the manual `sync` step — the agent gets fresh data the moment it connects. Should be non-blocking (serve immediately, sync in background) with a status tool indicating sync progress.

Add composite MCP tool `research_topic` that wraps the common search→traverse→retrieve workflow into a single tool call. Keeps individual tools intact but provides a one-shot convenience for the 80% case: (1) search_local_docs or search_semantic based on query, (2) auto-traverse top_k results 1-2 hops, (3) deduplicate, (4) return enriched results with full content + related context. Reduces 4-6 round-trips to 1 for the typical agent research pattern.

Add `--json` flag to every CLI command that outputs results in JSON-RPC 2.0 format (matching MCP server response structure) so agents can consume CLI output identically to MCP tool responses. Also add a `graphtor-docs manifest` command that emits a JSON-RPC 2.0 tool manifest listing all CLI commands with names, descriptions, and parameter schemas — mirroring what the MCP server returns via `tools/list` on initialization. This enables CLI-first agent workflows without requiring the MCP STDIO server, and ensures parity between CLI and MCP surfaces.

Update project documentation (README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/) to incorporate latest feature additions: --json global flag for JSON-RPC 2.0 CLI output, manifest subcommand, zero-config workspace adoption (init/install/doctor/upgrade/uninstall), and docs rebranding from LocalDocRAG to graphtor-docs. Ensure usage examples, architecture references, and CLI command listings reflect the current tool surface.

Replace brute-force O(n) vector search with CozoDB native HNSW index for sub-logarithmic approximate nearest-neighbor lookup. Current implementation loads all embeddings from doc_vectors as JSON strings, deserializes, computes cosine similarity in Rust, and sorts — O(n) per query. HNSW would provide O(log n) search, eliminate JSON serde overhead, and enable scaling to the full 703-repo MS Docs corpus (500k+ chunks). Requires schema v3 migration, native vector column type, and re-ingestion pass.

Includes read-only parallel access for search/status operations, per-database locking strategy, and graceful error recovery instead of panics when locks are encountered.

Source registry normalization and duplicate-intake preflight: Support multiple named source files (*.sources.yaml pattern e.g. graph.sources.yaml, powerbi.sources.yaml). Enforce consistent schema across all source files including explicit database field. Before ingestion, parse all source files and detect duplicate file/path intake across databases, alerting the operator to allow override or adjustment.

Serve safety: when an existing .db is used without .graphtor/config/sources.yaml, auto-generate a local stub config (sources: []) instead of falling back to workspace auto-discovery/background sync so imported databases can be served read-only without ingesting local markdown.
Run a full release-version test using the current .graphtor/config sources.yaml files, diagnose sync embedding-model lookup failures, and add useful sync progress indication to the sync command.

Cross-source cross-product link resolution in graph traversal.

PROBLEM: doc_edges { src_chunk_id, target_path => link_text, anchor } (src/db/edges.rs) stores link targets as raw strings. find_related_chunks (src/db/traverse.rs) resolves each target_path only against doc_chunks where source_id = seed.source_id AND path == target_path — deliberately source-scoped. So cross-product links (absolute Learn URL paths like /fabric/admin, and any link whose target lives in a different ingested source) never resolve; a multi-source DB is fragmented at source boundaries for graph traversal. (Vector search in src/db/search.rs is already cross-source; this is graph-edge-only.)

GOAL: Let traversal follow an edge whose target is a document in a different source when a reliable, globally-unique key identifies that target — without reintroducing the relative-path ambiguity the current source-scoping prevents.

CROSS-SOURCE KEY (contract with docline): Introduce a canonical_url identifier per chunk/doc, populated from a new docline frontmatter field canonical_url (the Learn URL a doc publishes under, e.g. /fabric/admin/foo, forward-slash, no host). Index it as a new relation, e.g. doc_url_index { canonical_url: String => source_id: String, chunk_id: String } (or a canonical_url column on doc_chunks plus a lookup). canonical_url MUST be globally unique across sources.

TWO-TIER RESOLUTION (in chunks_at_path / a new resolver): Tier 1 (unchanged): intra-source exact match — source_id = seed.source_id AND path == target_path. Keeps within-repo relative links fast and preserves the source-pollution guard. Tier 2 (new): if target_path is absolute (starts_with('/')) or Tier 1 returns nothing, look up doc_url_index by canonical_url == target_path — not source-scoped — resolving to (target_source_id, target_chunk_id).

TRAVERSAL CHANGES (find_related_chunks): after Tier-1, for unresolved/absolute targets call the new global chunk_by_canonical_url(target_path); enqueue the resolved chunk with its own source_id so subsequent hops are scoped correctly to the doc's home source. Respect max_depth. Unresolved target stays a dangling edge (no crash, no false match).

EDGE TYPING (recommended): classify each edge as intra_source vs cross_product (absolute target, or resolved to a different source_id) so consumers can weight/filter cross-repo hops.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) Two sources (e.g. powerbi + fabric) in one DB: a /fabric/admin/foo link from a powerbi chunk resolves via find_related_chunks to the fabric chunk (different source_id) when a matching canonical_url exists. (2) Intra-source relative links resolve exactly as before — no regression; identical relative source_paths across sources are NOT cross-linked. (3) Cross-product links with no matching canonical_url remain dangling (graceful). (4) Traversal hops across sources up to max_depth; anchors on cross-product edges are preserved.

OUT OF SCOPE: Deriving canonical_url (docline owns that). Changing vector search. Rewriting stored link text.

TOUCH POINTS: src/db/schema.rs (new relation/column + migration), src/db/edges.rs (index population), src/db/traverse.rs (chunks_at_path, find_related_chunks), src/parse/frontmatter.rs (read canonical_url if keying off frontmatter), src/db/chunks.rs (carry canonical_url).

Chore: reduce CI build actions to only run on code changes, to conserve GitHub Actions usage limits.

IDEA: The CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) currently runs the full build/fmt/clippy/test/audit pipeline on every PR/push, including chore/docs-only PRs where compilation is unnecessary. Skip the heavy build actions where they add no value.

APPROACHES TO CONSIDER:
- paths-ignore: on the workflow triggers to skip runs when only non-code paths change (e.g. docs/**, **/*.md, .github/agents/**, .github/instructions/**, .github/prompts/**).
- PR-title-based conditional gating on jobs/steps, e.g.:
    if: |
      !startsWith(github.event.pull_request.title, 'chore:') &&
      !startsWith(github.event.pull_request.title, 'docs:')
  to skip build actions for chore:/docs: PRs.
- Or a combination of path filters + title-based skip.

GOAL: Only run heavy build/clippy/test/audit actions when code actually changes, reducing GitHub Actions minutes/usage.

CAVEATS TO ADDRESS DURING DESIGN:
- Required status checks + branch protection: if the build check is a REQUIRED check, skipping the job (job never runs) can BLOCK merge because the required check never reports a conclusion. Options: use workflow-level paths/paths-ignore filters (GitHub treats path-skipped required checks as passing) rather than per-job if:; or add a companion job that reports success on skip; or make the check non-required. Design must not deadlock merges of chore/docs PRs.
- push to main should still run full CI (or at least on release-relevant changes).
- Keep the audit gate running whenever Cargo.lock / Cargo.toml change (advisory gate) even for chore/docs PRs.
- Title-based gating is fragile (PR title can change after checks run) and spoofable; path-based filtering is more robust — weigh both.

TOUCH POINTS: .github/workflows/ci.yml (triggers, job-level if / paths-ignore).

Console UX: when the embedding model directory cannot be found/loaded, print the diagnostic to the console in TTY red so the user clearly understands the model was missing (and that sync therefore degraded to graph-only with no vector embeddings).

Context / root cause: src/embed/resolver.rs emits the "[embed] local embedding model unavailable" / "[embed] embedding model unavailable" diagnostics via plain uncolored eprintln! (emit_local_dir_diagnostic ~L215-231, emit_resolution_diagnostic ~L193-210). On load failure resolve_embedding_model() degrades to Ok(None) and sync continues WITHOUT embeddings (doc_chunks.embedding stays null), which silently produces a graph/keyword-only index. A real user hit this and did not realize embeddings were skipped.

Desired behavior:
- Render the missing/unloadable embedding-model diagnostic in bold red on a TTY (auto-detected, honoring NO_COLOR), consistent with the new src/cli/errfmt.rs anstream/anstyle color approach (AutoStream strips ANSI on non-TTY). Note: the diagnostic lives in the graphtor-core lib (embed module), while errfmt is in the bin crate — either move a small shared color helper into the lib or add anstream/anstyle usage in the embed module.
- Also make the degraded outcome prominent at end of sync (e.g., a colored WARN summary line like "embeddings skipped — semantic search unavailable; N chunks stored without vectors") so the skip is not easily missed among logs.

Acceptance: on a TTY with a missing GRAPHTOR_EMBED_MODEL_DIR (or absent model files), sync prints a clearly red warning that embeddings were skipped; piped/non-TTY output is plain (NO_COLOR respected); existing tests still pass. Related to the error-messaging color work (errfmt) shipped for the fatal-error path.

Read-only, zero-config graphtor context server for agent workspaces (docline generates content -> graphtor builds the db -> agents consume it read-only), with the graphtor dev workspace as the generation+serve exception.

PRODUCT FRAMING (authoritative intent, per operator):
graphtor is not primarily a sync engine inside an agent environment. Pipeline: docline authors the standardized Markdown source; graphtor `sync` is a GENERATION-side step that builds a .db from that content (run where the docline content lives); the generated .db is consumed in AGENT workspaces as a READ-ONLY source of context. In a consumer workspace there is no source content, so graphtor should never sync there (sync there is only ever accidental). Modes are separated by ROLE:
  - Generation (authoring/build workspace, has docline output/sources): `sync` content -> .db (write).
  - Consumption (agent workspace, has only .db files): `serve` read-only context (no sync).

WORKSPACE-MODE EXCEPTION (critical): read-only consumption is the DEFAULT for ALL workspaces EXCEPT the graphtor tool's own development workspace (this repo, e.g. C:\Source\GitHub\graphtor). That one workspace is BOTH a generator AND a server — it must retain the full sync/write path (it builds/tests databases like powerbi.db, postgresql.db from its own sources.yaml). Every OTHER workspace is effectively a read-only server.
Mode-detection recommendation: derive mode from CONTENT, not a hardcoded path — a workspace is in generation mode only when it has RESOLVABLE ingestion sources with real content (sources.yaml with local sources whose paths exist). Otherwise it is read-only consumption, EVEN IF a stale/empty sources.yaml exists (a consumer workspace must never accidentally re-enable sync). The graphtor dev repo qualifies for generation because it has real sources; consumer workspaces (bare .db files, no real sources) get read-only auto-discovery. Consider an explicit override flag only as a safety escape hatch, but default behaviour must be content-derived and safe (fail read-only).

DESIGN IMPLICATION: read-only serve is the default posture; the write/sync posture is enabled only by presence of real generation sources (the dev workspace being the primary such case). An agent/consumer workspace's `serve` needs no sources.yaml and no GRAPHTOR_DB_PATH; it exposes whatever .db files live in `.graphtor/`, read-only.

Current behaviour (verified):
- `.mcp.json` from install is ALREADY minimal — managed_server_value (src/workspace/mcp_config.rs:273) writes only {command, args:["serve"], transport:"stdio"}, NO env. GRAPHTOR_DB_PATH/GRAPHTOR_SOURCES are operator-added by hand.
- No env -> `serve` defaults db_path=cwd/.graphtor/graph.db, config=cwd/.graphtor/config/sources.yaml.
- `serve` discovers dbs via discover_db_files(db_path, source_config) (src/main.rs:2408): iterates config.sources OR a single explicit db_path; does NOT scan `.graphtor/` for dropped .db files.
- `serve` opens each db read-write (rw_stores) AND read-only (ro_stores) via open_serve_databases (src/main.rs:2344) and spawns background incremental sync (WRITE) when sources.yaml has sources (src/main.rs:2447) — the accidental-resync risk.

Desired UX:
- Drop a .db into the root of `.graphtor/` -> `serve` auto-detects and exposes it read-only for query/search/semantic. No sources.yaml, no GRAPHTOR_DB_PATH.
- Source-backed dbs (a `local` source with an existing path) keep read-write + background sync (generation side); dbs with NO matching real source are served READ-ONLY and NEVER background-synced (no rescan, no v4 prune).

Design directions to deliberate:
A) serve auto-discovery of `*.db` in top level of `.graphtor/`; classify has-real-ingestion-source (rw + sync) vs no-source (read-only, no sync). Read-only default; sync only when real sources resolve.
B) Explicit read-only db entry in sources.yaml (new `type: database` kind, or top-level `databases:` list, or `read_only: true`) for external/aliased dbs.
C) Combination: auto-discovery zero-config default + explicit entries for named/aliased/external dbs.
Decide: consumption vs generation is CONTENT-DERIVED (resolvable real sources) by default; optional explicit override flag as escape hatch only.

Cross-cutting: serve db discovery + role classification; background-sync gating (never sync a no-real-source db, even with a stale sources.yaml); DataStore read-only open (open_sqlite_readonly exists); v4 pre-sync gate still applies to served read-only dbs (refuse/report pre-v4); MCP tool surface + list-sources across multiple auto-discovered dbs (synthesize source metadata from stored doc_sources); status parity; docs (.mcp.json, .graphtor layout, docline->graphtor->agent pipeline + dev-workspace exception, in product-specs/design-docs); security (only .graphtor root, path/containment, skip lock/index/tmp + .graphtor/models + generated artifacts); backward compat (default graph.db + existing sources-driven multi-db serve preserved for the generation/dev workspace).

Acceptance (high level): in a consumer workspace with a minimal .mcp.json (just `serve`) and .db files in `.graphtor/`, the MCP tools + `status` query them read-only and `serve` never writes/resyncs; in the graphtor dev workspace (real sources), sync still works and it can both generate and serve; a stale/empty sources.yaml in a consumer workspace does NOT enable sync; pre-v4 dbs are gated; docs capture the pipeline + dev-workspace exception. Deliberation first, then phased implementation.

Consumption-first `install`: default to a minimal serve-only footprint; make ingestion scaffolding opt-in; document ingestion setup separately.

Motivation / product framing: graphtor in a consumer (agent) workspace is a READ-ONLY context server, not a sync engine (see stash 79B5A7BC). Installing into a new workspace should therefore NOT scaffold ingestion machinery by default. Only the graphtor dev/authoring workspace (with real docline sources) needs the generation/sync scaffold.

Current behaviour (verified):
- `install()` (src/workspace/install.rs:34-45) creates ALL of `.graphtor/{bin,data,cache,config,logs}` from GRAPHTOR_SUBDIRS (src/workspace/paths.rs: GRAPHTOR_SUBDIRS = ["bin","data","cache","config","logs"]) and copies the running binary into `.graphtor/bin/`.
- cmd_install (src/main.rs:3002) then calls init_sources_yaml (src/main.rs:3018 -> src/workspace/init.rs) writing a template `.graphtor/config/sources.yaml`, and generate_mcp_config (src/main.rs:3028) writing/merging `.mcp.json`.
- Post-install message (src/main.rs:3080) tells the user to "edit .graphtor/config/sources.yaml to add documentation sources" — ingestion-oriented.
- Note: bin/data/cache/config/logs all support ingestion/generation; serve only needs the .graphtor root (to hold dropped .db files) + a resolvable binary + .mcp.json.

Desired behaviour:
- `install` default (consumption-first): create only what serve needs — the `.graphtor/` root (where operators drop .db files) and a minimal `.mcp.json` (command graphtor-docs, args ["serve"]). Do NOT write sources.yaml. Do NOT create config/bin/cache/data/logs. Post-install message should explain "drop a .db into .graphtor/ to serve it read-only" and link to the ingestion-setup docs.
- Ingestion/generation scaffold becomes OPT-IN: e.g. `graphtor-docs install --with-ingestion` (or the existing `graphtor-docs init` / a dedicated setup command) creates config + sources.yaml + data/cache/logs (+ bin/binary copy if used) for authoring/build workspaces. The graphtor dev workspace uses this path.
- Binary resolution for serve: consumption workspaces typically use a globally-installed `graphtor-docs` on PATH (so no `.graphtor/bin/` copy needed); .mcp.json should reference the PATH command by default, and only use `.graphtor/bin/graphtor-docs` when the ingestion/bin scaffold was created. Decide the resolution/precedence.

Documentation: add a SEPARATE docs section covering how to set up ingestion/sync of docline-produced source content (generation-side): creating the ingestion scaffold, authoring sources.yaml, running sync, and how the generated .db is then consumed read-only in agent workspaces. Keep the default install docs focused on the consumption/serve path.

Cross-cutting / considerations: install/uninstall/upgrade parity (uninstall must clean up whichever footprint was created; upgrade of a consumption install has no bin copy to replace); doctor expectations (doctor currently assumes config/data etc. — must tolerate the minimal consumption layout); idempotency; backward compat for existing full installs; the graphtor dev workspace must retain the full generation scaffold; .gitignore/.graphtor artifact expectations. Depends on / pairs with 79B5A7BC (serve read-only auto-discovery of .graphtor/*.db) — a minimal consumption install only makes sense once serve auto-discovers dropped dbs; sequence 79B5A7BC first or ship together.

Acceptance (high level): `graphtor-docs install` in a fresh consumer workspace creates only `.graphtor/` + a minimal serve `.mcp.json`, no sources.yaml and no config/bin/cache/data/logs; dropping a .db into `.graphtor/` makes it queryable read-only (via 79B5A7BC); an explicit opt-in flag/command scaffolds the ingestion/generation layout; uninstall cleans up correctly; docs have a distinct ingestion/sync setup section; the graphtor dev workspace keeps full generation capability.

cmd_upgrade lacks the is_reparse_point containment guard that install/uninstall/serve now have. In src/main.rs cmd_upgrade acquires WorkspaceLock::acquire(workspace_dir, force_unlock) on a workspace resolved by find_workspace_dir, which matches .graphtor via candidate.is_dir() (follows symlinks/junctions). If .graphtor is a reparse point pointing outside the project, upgrade's lock acquire and --force-unlock create/remove/replace graphtor.lock inside the external target (out-of-workspace mutation), the same containment class fixed for install (W7-1) and uninstall (W7-2) on PR 90. Fix: add if graphtor_core::path::is_reparse_point(and ws_dir) bail before the acquire in cmd_upgrade, mirroring the install/uninstall guards, plus a regression test planting a symlinked .graphtor and asserting upgrade fails closed and the linked target lock is untouched. Source: PR 90 wave-7 Security Reviewer finding, confidence 0.72, P3 advisory. ## Feature: Shared external read-only databases via `.graphtor/config/read-sources.yaml`

### Problem

Today `graphtor-docs` binds all database resolution (via `validate_path`) to the
invoking process's current working directory — enforced across `open_sqlite`,
`open_sqlite_readonly`, and `open_engine_readonly` in `src/db/store.rs`, all of
which pass `cwd` as the allowed root. This means a large (~1GB) shared database
(e.g., domain knowledge like Power BI docs) cannot be referenced read-only from
multiple separate dev-workspace directories on the same devbox without
duplicating the file — `--db-path`/`GRAPHTOR_DB_PATH` accept arbitrary paths but
are still validated against `cwd`, and symlinks/junctions are explicitly
rejected (`is_reparse_point` guard, canonicalization in `validate_path` follows
links to their real target and fails containment).

Actual operator workflow that motivates this: `sync` (write) is only ever run
outside any dev workspace, against a dedicated build location. Inside any dev
workspace, only read-only serving/querying is ever needed. Given that, the
generic "any file the process touches must live under this one cwd" rule is
broader than the actual risk surface for this specific read-only use case.

This was previously scoped and explicitly deferred, not overlooked — see
`docs/design-docs/2026-07-15-consumption-first-serve-and-trust-boundary.md`:
"Like auto-discovered entries, an explicit `type: database` path must stay
within the workspace root ... external-path support is out of scope for this
phase." The original `docs/decisions/2026-05-22-multi-database-file-support-deliberation.md`
even named "cross-project reuse without re-sync" as requirement R4, suggesting
"symlink or path reference" — later security hardening (the `is_reparse_point`
guard, PR #90) closed that specific path.

### Proposed design

New file: `.graphtor/config/read-sources.yaml` — separate from `sources.yaml`
(the ingestion/sync registry) on purpose:

* `sources.yaml` is plausibly team-committed and drives `sync` (write path).
* `read-sources.yaml` is inherently devbox-local (points at absolute local
  paths that won't exist on another machine/checkout) and should default to
  **gitignored**. It drives `serve`/query only — never sync.

Proposed schema (absolute paths only, no relative-to-cwd ambiguity):

```yaml
databases:
  - path: C:\Users\me\graphtor-shared\powerbi.db
    label: powerbi   # optional, for status/diagnostics output
  - path: C:\Users\me\graphtor-shared\rust-docs.db
```

Validation rules distinct from `validate_path`'s workspace-root containment:

* Path must be absolute — reject relative entries outright.
* Path must exist and be a regular file, not a symlink/junction
  (`is_reparse_point` check) — defends against TOCTOU repointing after the
  operator approves an entry.
* Reject `..` traversal components even in absolute form.

Wiring: union these entries into `discover_served_databases`'s output under a
**new posture** (e.g. `ExternalReadOnly`), always opened via
`open_engine_readonly`, and — critically — never eligible for `Generation`
promotion under any circumstance, so a `read-sources.yaml` entry can never
become a sync target even by accident.

### Security analysis already done (do not re-litigate from scratch)

* This touches Constitution Principle III/IV (workspace isolation / CLI
  containment), which is NON-NEGOTIABLE in this repo's governance model — a
  proper `deliberate`/ADR pass is required before implementation, not just a
  code change.
* The relevant risk is NOT "write vs. read" — it's that MCP tool read results
  (`get_document`, `get_chunk`, `search`, `search_semantic`) flow directly into
  the LLM/agent's context. Relaxing containment for reads is itself an
  information-disclosure/exfiltration vector (aligns with the constitution's
  own Principle III rationale: "could ... leak internal paths, or expose
  sensitive information"), not a lower-risk variant of the write-path concern.
* The explicit-opt-in, separate-file, devbox-local/gitignored design is the
  right shape specifically because it matches the existing documented "operator
  trust boundary" philosophy (`docs/design-docs/2026-07-15-consumption-first-serve-and-trust-boundary.md`):
  "Only drop `.db` files ... from sources you trust" — an explicit, deliberate,
  local decision, not something silently expanded via ingestion config, an env
  var, or a bare `--db-path` override.
* Mechanical note: CozoDB's SQLite backend always opens
  `SQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE|CREATE`; graphtor's own "read-only" is entirely an
  app-level (`AccessMode`) + filesystem-level (`EngineReadonlyGuard` chmod)
  construction, not an engine-native guarantee — worth keeping in mind when
  reasoning about blast radius of any bypass.

### Known implementation gap to fix as part of this work

`EngineReadonlyGuard` (`src/db/store.rs`) captures/restores original file
permissions per guard instance with **no cross-process reference counting**.
Concretely, with two separate `graphtor-docs serve`/query processes (e.g. two
dev-workspace MCP server instances) both opening the *same* shared external db
read-only concurrently:

1. Process A opens first (file writable → marks readonly, remembers
   original=writable).
2. Process B opens second while A is still open (file already readonly →
   marks readonly again, remembers original=readonly).
3. A finishes first and drops its guard → restores its captured original:
   **writable**, while B's `DataStore` is still alive and still reports
   `is_engine_enforced_readonly() == true`.
4. Any new lazily-opened pooled connection Cozo creates in B's process after
   step 3 opens against a now-writable file and gets genuine read-write access
   — B's read-only guarantee has silently gone stale.

Not a SQLite-integrity risk by itself (WAL's own reader/writer coordination is
unaffected, and in the stated workflow no writer is ever active concurrently
with these reads), but it means "engine-enforced read-only" isn't actually true
under multi-process concurrent access as implemented today. Should be fixed
with a proper cross-process refcount (e.g. a small advisory counter file per
shared db path, incremented on guard-acquire, only restoring permissions when
it drops to zero) rather than left as a latent gap once this feature makes
multi-process concurrent read genuinely common instead of incidental.
